title: Classic Traveller star map record
description: A star map generated from Book 3 Worlds and Adventures pp. 1-12: either the p. 3 sub-sector grid, or the sector of sixteen of them (ERRATA E006). This schema describes the record the engine writes at milestone 3: the world occurrence scan, starport types, naval and scout bases, routes, and the eight characteristics of every world. It grows with each milestone that adds fields, all of it at schema_version 1, because pre-release growth invalidates no released record.

schema_version.description: The shape of the record. Bumps when a constraint would invalidate a record the current engine writes.

engine_version.description: Bumps for a rule change, a change to dice-stream consumption order, or a change to the RNG construction, and for nothing else.

seed.description: Fills both words of the PCG state, so this one field reproduces the stream. A seed the engine drew is at most 2^53-1 so that a reader parsing JSON numbers as doubles cannot round it; an explicit --seed may be any uint64.

errata.description: The readings that actually governed this record, in document order. Each entry in ERRATA.md states its own stamping condition.

notes.description: The referee's own note about the map as a whole. Never generated and never read back; absent from a record that has none (issue 1 #6).

occurrence_dm.description: The referee's world occurrence DM, applied to the whole subsector (p. 1).

grid.description: The hex grid the hexes below are numbered on: 8x10 for the p. 3 sub-sector grid, 32x40 for a sector of sixteen of them (ERRATA E006). A record written before grids were recorded has none, and is a sub-sector. The pair is what is named, not the two dimensions separately -- 8x40 and 32x10 are grids nothing prints and starmap.Decode refuses, so the oneOf below is what keeps the schema from accepting a record the reader rejects.

routes.description: The commercial routes of p. 2, in ascending hex number of the first world and then of the second (ERRATA E003).

hex.description: The four-digit column-and-row number the p. 3 grid prints. 0101 through 0810 on a sub-sector grid; up to 3240 on a sector grid (ERRATA E006). The record's grid says which.

name.description: Always empty: p. 12 step 3 says to name each world and prints no table, so the hex identifies it.

notes.description: The referee's own note about this world. Never generated and never read back; absent from a world that has none (issue 1 #6).

naval_base.description: The p. 5 chart prints a naval base throw at starports A and B only; elsewhere this is false without a throw having been made.

scout_base.description: The p. 5 chart prints a scout base throw at starports A through D; elsewhere this is false without a throw having been made.

atmosphere.description: 2D-7 + size; automatically 0 at size 0, with no die thrown (R13). Nothing caps it at the p. 5 table's last row: a value no table names is a gap in the table, not a bound on the throw (ERRATA E004).

hydrographics.description: 2D-7 + size, with a further DM of -4 if the atmosphere is 0, 1, or greater than 9; automatically 0 at size 0 or 1, with no die thrown (R13).

law_level.description: 2D-7 + government (pp. 8, 12). Government feeds this already floored.

tech_index.description: One die plus the sum of the p. 9 matrix DMs. The one value the book prints a range for rather than a table that happens to end: zero to 18 (p. 9).

digits.description: The string of digits of p. 4: the starport type and the seven characteristics, eight characters, nothing between them. The familiar hyphen is not in the held text (ERRATA E005). The alphabet is Book 1 p. 8's hexadecimal extended by Book 3 p. 2's letters, omitting O and I.

clamps.description: The floor or the cap that actually bound, absent where nothing did. Raw is the one thing here that cannot be recomputed from a value.

characteristic.description: Starport is not among them: it is a table lookup and never arithmetic, so it can never be clamped.

from.description: The lower hex identifier of the pair. A route is not directed; ordering the pair is what keeps one route from being written two ways.

distance.description: The jump distance in parsecs. The jump routes table states a target only at 1 through 4, so no route exists beyond four hexes.
